Use this reference for Domain 1. The returned question cards supply the exact
wording, allowed answer values, guidance, and activation rules.

Keep three propositions separate:

1. **Sequence generation:** Was the allocation sequence random?
2. **Allocation concealment:** Was allocation concealed until participants were
   enrolled and assigned?
3. **Baseline differences:** Do observed imbalances suggest a problem with the
   randomization process rather than chance?

Sequence methods such as computer generation, random-number tables, lots, or
minimization may support the first proposition. Identify the random component;
concealing a predictable formula does not make it random.

assignment. When reported facts support a probable judgment, state the inferred
safeguard or weakness. Preserve `no_information` when the details and trial
circumstances do not support that judgment.

list and any explanation. Different values are not automatically evidence of a
randomization problem. Missing reporting is not evidence that randomization
failed.

list-introducing sentence alone does not answer these questions.

inventory to include appendices, supplements, or combined documents that may
describe the actual sequence or concealment procedure. Search with concrete
study wording from the report. Continue a cursor, issue another bounded query,

procedure before selecting Evidence. Stop when the complete premise is
supported or record the bounded information limit. Source role, an unopened
document, and a no-hit query do not establish how allocation was performed.

4|docetaxel given at the time ADT was initiated for
5|hormone-sensitive disease resulted in better can-
6|cer control than that with ADT alone, with a
7|longer time to the development of castration resis-
8|tance, a higher rate of decrease of the PSA level
9|to less than 0.2 ng per milliliter at 12 months, a
10|lower number of prostate-cancer deaths, and
11|substantially longer overall survival. The longer
12|overall survival than that with ADT alone was
13|achieved despite the fact that almost half the 287
14|patients who received ADT alone and then met
15|the criteria for castration resistance received
16|docetaxel at the time of disease progression
17|along with other therapies that prolong overall
18|survival in patients with metastatic castration-
19|resistant prostate cancer.
20|The definition of high-volume disease used
21|for this protocol was a combination of features
22|from prior classifications. All the definitions
23|included the presence of nonnodal, soft-tissue
24|visceral disease as a predictor of poor prognosis.
25|This protocol made use of sites of bone metas-
26|tases and the number of metastases to avoid
27|classifying patients with three or fewer sites as
28|having high-volume disease even if one lesion
29|was beyond the vertebrae and pelvis (any lesion
30|beyond the vertebrae and pelvis, irrespective of
31|total lesion count, would be classified as "exten-
32|sive" according to the definition of the South-
33|west Oncology Group4). In the subgroup of pa-
34|tients with high-volume disease, the median
35|overall survival was 17.0 months longer in the
36|combination group than in the ADT-alone group
37|(49.2 months vs. 32.2 months). On the basis of
38|an unpublished analysis of data from the S9346
39|trial5 we had projected a median survival of
40|33 months among patients with high-volume
41|disease (according to the definition used in our
42|protocol) in the ADT-alone group, and as such,
43|the definition was reproducible across two phase
44|3 studies conducted in a similar time period.
45|A previously reported randomized study in-
46|volving 380 patients (the GETUG-AFU 15 study),
47|which had a similar design to that of the current
48|study, did not detect longer overall survival with
49|combination therapy.10 The median overall sur-
50|vival was longer than in our study - 54.2 months
51|with ADT alone (which suggests that the study
52|had a different case mix than that in our study)
53|- and was first analyzed in 2011, before there
54|was widespread access to newer therapies that
55|have been shown to prolong overall survival
56|among patients with castration-resistant pros-
57|tate cancer. In the GETUG-AFU 15 study, the
58|time to progression was longer, the number of
59|prostate-cancer deaths was smaller, and the num-
60|ber of treatment-related deaths was larger (4 of
61|195 patients) with early docetaxel therapy than
62|with ADT alone. The Medical Research Council
63|STAMPEDE trial will add further data on the
64|role of docetaxel in hormone-sensitive prostate
65|cancer; to date, the overall survival in the ADT-

39|BACKGROUND
40|Androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT) has been the backbone of treatment for
41|metastatic prostate cancer since the 1940s. We assessed whether concomitant
42|treatment with ADT plus docetaxel would result in longer overall survival than that
43|with ADT alone.
44|METHODS
45|We assigned men with metastatic, hormone-sensitive prostate cancer to receive
46|either ADT plus docetaxel (at a dose of 75 mg per square meter of body-surface
47|area every 3 weeks for six cycles) or ADT alone. The primary objective was to test
48|the hypothesis that the median overall survival would be 33.3% longer among
49|patients receiving docetaxel added to ADT early during therapy than among pa-
50|tients receiving ADT alone.
51|RESULTS
52|A total of 790 patients (median age, 63 years) underwent randomization. After a
53|median follow-up of 28.9 months, the median overall survival was 13.6 months
54|longer with ADT plus docetaxel (combination therapy) than with ADT alone (57.6
55|months vs. 44.0 months; hazard ratio for death in the combination group, 0.61;
56|95% confidence interval [CI], 0.47 to 0.80; P<0.001). The median time to bio-
57|chemical, symptomatic, or radiographic progression was 20.2 months in the com-
58|bination group, as compared with 11.7 months in the ADT-alone group (hazard
59|ratio, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.51 to 0.72; P<0.001). The rate of a prostate-specific antigen
60|level of less than 0.2 ng per milliliter at 12 months was 27.7% in the combination
61|group versus 16.8% in the ADT-alone group (P<0.001). In the combination group,
62|the rate of grade 3 or 4 febrile neutropenia was 6.2%, the rate of grade 3 or 4
63|infection with neutropenia was 2.3%, and the rate of grade 3 sensory neuropathy
64|and of grade 3 motor neuropathy was 0.5%.
65|CONCLUSIONS
66|Six cycles of docetaxel at the beginning of ADT for metastatic prostate cancer re-
67|sulted in significantly longer overall survival than that with ADT alone. (Funded by
68|the National Cancer Institute and others; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00309985.)

10|to improve the efficacy or decrease the treatment

12|androgens alone, intermittent dosing of ADT,
13|and the use of an antiandrogen combined with
14|medical or surgical castration.2-4 A meta-analysis
15|revealed an increase in survival of 3 percentage
16|points at 5 years with concurrent use of a non-
17|steroidal antiandrogen at the time of initiation
18|of ADT.2 However, resistance to ADT occurs in
19|most patients, with the result that the median
20|survival among patients with metastatic prostate
21|cancer is approximately 3 years.5,6 In patients
22|with resistance to ADT, docetaxel therapy re-
23|sulted in a median survival that was approxi-

25|xantrone and prednisone.7,8
26|Prior studies of chemotherapy plus ADT, which
27|did not show a benefit, were small studies that
28|involved primarily patients with a relatively low
29|tumor burden.9,10 Definitions of a high burden of
30|disease have included the presence of visceral
31|metastases, a bone-metastasis burden categorized
32|by site (beyond the axial skeleton) or by a high
33|number of lesions, or a combination of these.9,11,12

35|ADT alone or ADT plus docetaxel at the begin-

40|Methods
41|Study Oversight
42|The primary objective of the E3805 study was to
43|determine whether docetaxel therapy at the be-
44|ginning of ADT for metastatic hormone-sensitive
45|prostate cancer would result in longer overall
46|survival than that with ADT alone. The study was
47|designed in 2005 by the Eastern Cooperative On-
48|cology Group (ECOG; now part of ECOG-ACRIN)
49|and was approved by the institutional review
50|board at each participating institution. The study
51|was coordinated by the ECOG-ACRIN Cancer
52|Research Group. The ECOG-ACRIN Statistical
53|Center collected the data and was the leading
54|cooperative group and data coordinating center.
55|The first two authors attest that the study was
56|conducted and monitored as specified by the
57|protocol. The first author wrote the first draft of
58|the manuscript, with subsequent contributions
59|by all the coauthors. The authors vouch for the
60|accuracy and completeness of the data presented.
61|The protocol with the statistical analysis plan
62|is available with the full text of this article at
63|NEJM.org. Sanofi donated the docetaxel for
64|early use (i.e., before progression during ADT)
65|and provided a grant to ECOG-ACRIN but had

# Assess deviations from intended interventions

Use this reference for Domain 2, which assesses the effect of assignment to
intervention. The returned question cards are authoritative.

For active conduct questions, build the chain in order:

1. What intervention was intended in each randomized group?
2. What change, non-adherence, or additional intervention occurred?
3. Did the trial context cause that change?
4. Could it affect the outcome, and was it balanced between groups?

For 2.3, a negative answer covers no relevant deviation as well as changes that
were protocol-consistent or could occur outside the trial context. An affirmative
answer needs evidence or strong reason linking a protocol-inconsistent deviation
to the trial context. State that link when it is an inference.
A protocol establishes the plan, not conduct. Different assigned treatments or
visible schedules do not by themselves prove that participants or carers knew
the assignment.

For 2.6, assess the analysis separately. Compare randomized assignment with the analyzed
population, exclusions, reassignment, and reasons. An ITT label is not proof
that all randomized participants were analyzed as assigned. Excluding only
participants with missing outcome data is not automatically the same as an
inappropriate assignment-effect analysis; keep that issue distinct for Domain
3. If an analysis defect activates the impact question, consider outcome rarity
and prognostic exclusions as well as the percentage affected.

Support each conduct-chain proposition with source facts and any stated
inference. A passage supporting one proposition does not settle the others.

# Assess missing outcome data

Use this reference for Domain 3. The approved Result fixes the outcome and time
point; the returned question cards fix answer direction and activation.

Every active answer is accompanied by a concise justification, an `unknowns`
array (use `[]` when none are identified), and a `counterevidence` array. A
counterpoint refers to the answer's zero-based basis index, for example:

```json
"counterevidence": [{"basis_index": 0, "implication": "This passage limits the strength of the selected answer."}]
```

Inactive branch answers may be omitted or retained without fabricated reasoning;
the server commits only the dependency-closed active path.

## Availability audit

For D3.1, support Yes or Probably Yes with actual outcome-availability
evidence. Accept one or more of:

- comparable observed-outcome counts for the randomized population;
- arm-specific loss-to-follow-up or censoring rates, reasons, and follow-up
  accounting; or
- an explicit statement that ascertainment was complete or nearly complete.

The following do not establish affirmative availability on their own:

- analysis denominators or ITT membership;
- planned or scheduled follow-up;
- treatment continuation or discontinuation; or
- a generic censoring rule without actual rates or follow-up accounting.

For mortality, recovery or discharge does not establish vital status at a later
time point. A total combining completed follow-up, recovery, and death does not
establish mortality availability. If availability remains unresolved, inspect
outcome-status or missing-value tables, including supplements. Match their
outcome and time window to the approved Result. Recovery may inform bias from
missingness, but does not make unknown vital status observed.

When the availability premise remains unresolved, use the active comparison
card's full Source inventory to inspect unopened supplements or combined
protocol documents. Search for concrete study wording such as the outcome
status, withdrawal or loss-to-follow-up labels, and the reported time point;
`missing outcome data` alone may not occur in the report. Widen the Source
scope or continue a cached cursor only as needed, and stop when comparable
observed counts or complete follow-up accounting are inspected. If the
captured Sources and bounded page windows do not establish availability,
document that limit instead of treating an empty Source group or a no-hit
search as evidence of missing outcomes.

## Reconcile availability

Keep these quantities distinct for each arm and time point:

- randomized participants;
- participants with the outcome observed;
- participants included in the reported analysis;
- participants whose outcomes were imputed; and
- post-randomization exclusions.

An analyzed count is not necessarily an observed count. Imputed outcomes count
as missing outcome data for RoB 2. Treatment discontinuation is not missing
outcome data when follow-up and outcome ascertainment continued.

If some outcomes are missing, assess whether data remain available for nearly
all randomized participants. Consider whether the missing outcomes could make
an important difference to this Result. For dichotomous outcomes, compare the
missing count with observed events, not only the randomized denominator.
A count below the randomized total does not settle that question.

Distinguish administrative censoring at a common data cutoff from censoring
caused by missing follow-up before the outcome could be observed. For time-to-event Results,
censoring may still create missing outcome information; assess its timing,
reason, and relation to treatment or prognosis instead of treating every
censored participant as either fully observed or missing by default.

Question 3.1 may include compact `missing_data` rows. Give each row a comparable
arm, population, unit, and time point. Use a row-level `basis` only to narrow or
add to the answer's Evidence. The server calculates differences and fractions
only after scopes match and preserves conflicting reports without choosing the
scientific answer.

When a count comparison would help before answering, call `get_domain_context`
with `missing_data` rows. Every preview row needs a nonempty `basis` containing
current-Trial Evidence references: no answer exists to supply inherited Evidence.
Inspect `comparison_cards[].missing_data`
for differences, fractions, and conflicting reports. The preview changes no
checkpoint or State revision. To retain the chosen rows, submit them with the
3.1 answer in `validate_domain_assessment`; omit row `basis` there only to reuse
the answer's Evidence when it supports those counts. After its receipt, save
the exact draft with `save_domain_judgment`.

Check each input against its source passage before using the arithmetic. The
helper subtracts supplied observed counts from randomized counts; it does not
extract counts or sum grouped departures. Keep unknown observed counts unknown.
Skip the preview when an explicit ascertainment statement resolves availability
without arithmetic.

## Assess bias from missingness

If data were not available for all or nearly all participants, ask in sequence:

1. Does a bias-correcting method or informative sensitivity analysis show that
   the Result was not biased?
2. Could missingness depend on the true outcome, based on reasons, health
   status, withdrawal, loss to follow-up, or censoring?
3. If it could, is that dependence likely given arm differences, reasons,
   prognostic factors, or trial circumstances?

Simple imputation, including last observation carried forward or multiple
imputation based only on intervention group, does not by itself show freedom from
bias. Documented reasons support reassurance only when they address the outcome
relationship.

Keep possible dependence in 3.3 separate from likely dependence in 3.4. For
3.4, state which reasons or trial circumstances support the likelihood judgment.
Absent contrary evidence alone does not establish likely dependence. Preserve
`no_information` when the card's uncertainty rule applies, even when that answer
leads to High risk of bias.

D3.2 does not allow `no_information`. When no bias-correcting evidence is found,
use the question card to choose a permitted negative or probably-negative answer
with the appropriate limitation or Evidence basis. Do not fabricate direct
support for the absence of bias.
